title: Cloudflare Tunnel
description: Publish apps through your server’s outbound connection. No inbound web ports required.
statusUnavailable: Could not load the current connection. Try again.
empty: Connect a named tunnel to manage custom domains, DNS and optional Access protection from Openship.
permissions: Token permissions: Zone Read, DNS Edit and Cloudflare Tunnel Edit. Access also requires Access Apps and Policies Edit.
convertTunnel: This tunnel is locally managed. Choose a remotely managed tunnel, or convert it in Cloudflare first.
name: Tunnel name
existingConnectorHint: cloudflared already runs on this deployment server.
installConnectorHint: Openship installs and manages its own connector on Linux.
autoDomainsHint: New custom domains on this server use this tunnel. Existing domains stay unchanged.
autoEnabled: New custom domains use this tunnel.
autoDisabled: Connect existing domains from their project’s domain settings.
defaultProtected: New domains require the selected Access policy.
protectHint: Require a reusable Allow or Service Auth policy. Openship creates an application for each hostname and keeps the policy in Cloudflare.
review: Only this setup’s Cloudflare resources are managed.
completeFields: Choose a credential, account and tunnel. Complete the required settings to connect.
disconnectHint: Unpublish this connection’s hostnames and remove its managed connector. Existing tunnels, reusable Access policies and unrelated resources are kept. Project domains remain configured for external ingress.
disconnectDomainHint: Remove this hostname’s managed DNS, tunnel rule and Access application. Its project route remains configured for external ingress.
noConnection: Connect a Cloudflare Tunnel on this project’s server first.
finishServer: Finish connecting the server’s tunnel before applying this hostname.
existingUnchanged: These defaults apply only to new domains. Existing hostnames keep their current Access policies.
